clue.text: Contemplated finding employment in Maryland

indicators.note: the word employment is placed in the middle of the state abbreviation

parts.note: MD is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maryland
employment is use, as in putting something to use

explanation.surface: Someone weighed up taking a job in Maryland.
explanation.definitionFit: To have mused is to have thought something over at length, so it is a synonym of contemplated.

clue.text: Party agenda with obvious appeal

parts.note: manifest means plain to see, obvious
O is the exclamation of appeal or invocation, as in 'O Lord'

explanation.surface: A political party's programme with plainly popular appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeal' looks like charm, but it is the vocative O used when calling on someone; 'with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A political party publishes its programme of policies before an election in this document.

clue.text: A monocle offers splendid sight

definitions.meaning: a single eyeglass, an old use of the singular word for glasses
an impressive public show or display

explanation.surface: Someone's eyeglass makes them look magnificent.
explanation.definitionFit: The singular word once named one lens or eyeglass, and also means an impressive display or show.

clue.text: So shines a good in a mighty world" (Merchant of Venice, Act V)

definitions.text: So shines a good in a mighty world" (Merchant of Venice, Act V)

parts.words: So shines a good in a mighty world" (Merchant of Venice, Act V)
parts.note: a quotation with its missing word left out: Portia's line about a small candle's light, the missing word being a good act

explanation.walkthrough: Portia says 'How far that little candle throws his beams! So shines a good deed in a naughty world'; the printed 'mighty' stands for Shakespeare's 'naughty', and the solver supplies the word that has dropped out after 'good'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Portia's line means an act or action, here a kindly one.

clue.text: Simple disagreement makes him bring a suit

parts.note: plain means simple, unadorned
a tiff is a minor quarrel or disagreement

explanation.surface: A petty row with someone drives him to take legal action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' sounds like clothing, but it is a lawsuit; 'makes' joins wordplay to a definition that describes the person who brings one.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, the party who brings a civil action against another is so called, the opposite of the defendant.

clue.text: Appear unwilling to make money by vigorous sportsmanship

definitions.meaning: to feign reluctance, especially in romance

definitions.text: to make money by vigorous sportsmanship
definitions.meaning: read literally: compete energetically in order to earn

explanation.surface: Someone is reluctant to earn a living through strenuous sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means feigning reluctance, and read word by word it also means competing hard in order to earn.

clue.text: Arrest results in prison

definitions.meaning: British slang: to arrest them
British slang for a prison or police station

explanation.surface: Being arrested ends with a jail term.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang the same word means to arrest someone and a jail or police station.

clue.text: One day I reverted to being a fool

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: reverted tells us the word to is turned round

parts.note: the word to taken as it is before reversal

explanation.surface: One day I slipped back into acting foolishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverted' looks like slipping back in behaviour, but it turns 'to' into OT; 'being' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a stupid person, a synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Elaborate idea

definitions.meaning: ornate, decorated
a notion or whim that takes one's ...

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means ornate or decorated, and the noun means a whim or notion.

clue.text: Relative's note in Riviera resort

definitions.note: read as 'relative is', the 's being a link

indicators.note: the note is placed in the middle of the resort's name

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A relative's postcard sent from a holiday on the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' suggests a letter home, but it is the musical note E; the 's of 'Relative's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member, a type of relative.

clue.text: During sale theology graduate clearly got carried away!

definitions.note: the noun names the act of a person being carried away by force

indicators.note: during tells us the graduate appears within the sale

parts.note: an auction is a public sale
BD is a Bachelor of Divinity, a degree in theology

explanation.surface: At an auction a divinity graduate plainly lost control of their emotions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried away' suggests excitement, but the definition is being taken away by force; 'clearly' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A kidnapping is someone being taken off by force, the literal sense of being carried away.

clue.text: The Princess of Wales is involved but impartial

parts.note: Di was the familiar name of Diana, Princess of Wales; Di is becomes Di's
interested means involved, having a stake

explanation.surface: Diana is taking part, yet stays neutral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is not a link here: 'Di is' contracts to DI'S, giving DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Disinterested means having no personal stake, hence unbiased or neutral.

clue.text: Lard and dripping for Mr Waller

definitions.meaning: both are animal cooking ...
... Waller was an American jazz pianist

explanation.surface: Cooking grease served up for a jazz pianist.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard and dripping are kinds of cooking fat, and Thomas Waller, the jazz pianist, had that nickname.

clue.text: A good entertainer needs spirit

parts.note: a host entertains guests

explanation.surface: A good party host needs plenty of liveliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests energy, but here it is a phantom.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost is a disembodied spirit or apparition.

clue.text: Continue to give support

definitions.meaning: remain, carry on
a ... is a prop or brace, and to ... is to support

explanation.surface: Keep on backing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means remain or carry on, and also to prop up, as a ship's mast is held by ropes.

clue.text: I don't believe you need to grow old!

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of disbelief
to ... is to age

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that ageing is necessary.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a cry of disbelief and also an idiom for ageing.

clue.text: A huge church initially in total disorder

indicators.note: initially says the church comes at the start of the answer

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A vast church at first in complete confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letters signal but places CH first; OS for outsize stands for huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaos is complete confusion, a state of total disorder.

clue.text: Banking institution preparing to move elsewhere

definitions.meaning: an establishment where banks settle cheques between one another
read literally: emptying one's home before moving

explanation.surface: A bank getting ready to relocate.
explanation.definitionFit: The financial office settles payments between banks, and read literally the phrase describes emptying a home before moving.

clue.text: Stress that it's south of the Equator

definitions.meaning: to emphasise, as by drawing a line beneath
read literally: below the Line, an old name for the Equator

explanation.surface: Emphasising that something lies in the southern hemisphere.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise a point is the verb's sense, and the Equator is often called the Line, so whatever is south of it sits below the Line.

clue.text: A rose elegant in shape

indicators.note: putting the letters into shape means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A rose that is stylish in form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in shape' looks like a description of the rose; 'shape' rearranges ELEGANT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild flowering plant of the rose family.

clue.text: Last drink for a dedicated traveller

definitions.meaning: a final drink before leaving
read literally: someone devoted to the open road

explanation.surface: A final drink for a committed wayfarer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the final drink before setting off home, and read literally a person devoted to the highway.

clue.text: Catch one's breath and talk quietly

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: Someone pauses for air and then speaks in a soft voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasp is a sudden sharp intake of air.

clue.text: Augustus has to display enthusiasm

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Augustus has to display enthusiasm' gives GUST in Augustus but no reading yields the closing O without a word doing two jobs; likely an OCR or transcription fault in the clue.

clue.text: Fast writer

definitions.meaning: quick, speedy
Jonathan ..., author of Gulliver's Travels

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means quick, and Jonathan Swift was the satirical author of Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Extraordinarily eager to give consent

indicators.note: extraordinarily signals the letters of eager are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Very keen to say yes.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to assent or say yes to a proposal.

clue.text: She joined the Navy as an architect

definitions.meaning: a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service
Sir Christopher ..., designer of St Paul's Cathedral

explanation.surface: A woman enlisted in the Navy in the role of architect.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Women's Royal Naval Service bore this name, as did Sir Christopher, who designed St Paul's Cathedral.

clue.text: Refuse container offered by the captain

definitions.meaning: in Britain a large open bin for builders' rubbish
informal short form of skipper, a team or ship's captain

explanation.surface: The captain provides a rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip is the British name for a large open rubbish container left outside building works.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain it is a large open bin for rubbish, and it is also short for skipper, a captain.

clue.text: Dog food

definitions.meaning: a Chinese breed with a blue-black tongue
informal word for grub, nosh

explanation.surface: Something to feed the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Chinese breed with a blue-black tongue, and also slang for grub.

clue.text: Keep trying to impale a songbird

parts.note: to stick is to pierce or impale
the tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Someone persistently tries to spear a little bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means persevere or keep going with something.

clue.text: Henry and I go round small island in the Caribbean

definitions.note: a definition by location: a country found in that sea

indicators.note: go round says Henry and I enclose the island

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
an ait is a small river island

explanation.surface: Henry and I sail round a tiny island in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: An AIT (or eyot) is a small island in a river such as the Thames; the definition names the answer by where it lies.
explanation.definitionFit: The country shares the island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic, in that sea.

clue.text: Extensive alfresco banquet

parts.note: alfresco means outdoors, out
a spread is a lavish meal

explanation.surface: A large open-air feast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stretched wide and fully opened out is extensive.

clue.text: A question of position

parts.note: the interrogative word one uses to ask about location

explanation.definitionFit: The interrogative asks about place or location.
